Agent Name: Planner
, Step Number: 2
, Reason for Mistake: In the second step (the first Planner response after the initial WebSurfer search), the Planner incorrectly assumed that the town associated with John the Hairy was "Rostov" and immediately hypothesized it referred to either Rostov Veliky or Rostov-on-Don. Crucially, the Planner failed to verify the specific location of the historical figure before making this assumption. The initial WebSurfer results only stated "Rostov" without disambiguation, and the Planner jumped to a conclusion that "Rostov typically maps to Rostov-on-Don in modern sources" without evidence. This premature assumption led to a cycle of redundant searches where the WebSurfer was repeatedly instructed to check for "Rostov Veliky" vs "Rostov-on-Don," despite the fact that the actual answer (that John the Hairy is associated with Rostov Veliky) was available in the very first set of search results (the Wikipedia snippet explicitly said "John the Merciful of Rostov" and later searches confirmed the connection to Rostov Veliky via Russian sources like "Rostov Kremlin" and "Church of the All-Holy" which are in Rostov Veliky). The Planner's failure to analyze the nuance of the initial results or to instruct the WebSurfer to open the specific Wikipedia page for "John the Hairy" to read the full context caused the prolonged ambiguity and inefficiency.
